strategy_name: ICT Inner Circle Trading with Fibonacci Retracement
description: Professional trading strategy combining ICT concepts with Fibonacci retracement for high-probability setups

risk_reward_ratio.description: Never take trades below 1:2 RR. Aim for 1:3 when possible

position_sizing.description: Risk only 1-2% of total capital per trade

stop_loss_rules.placement: Below/above the order block or fair value gap that created the setup
stop_loss_rules.buffer: Add 2-5 pips buffer beyond the structure to avoid stop hunts
stop_loss_rules.never: Never move stop loss against your position

trend_identification.bullish: Series of higher highs (HH) and higher lows (HL)
trend_identification.bearish: Series of lower highs (LH) and lower lows (LL)
trend_identification.rule: Only trade in the direction of the higher timeframe trend

timeframe_alignment.rule: HTF trend must align with LTF setup

break_of_structure.choch: Change of character - potential reversal signal
break_of_structure.rule: Wait for BOS in trend direction before looking for entries

order_blocks.definition: Last bullish candle before bearish move (or vice versa)
order_blocks.bullish_ob: Last down candle before strong move up - acts as support
order_blocks.bearish_ob: Last up candle before strong move down - acts as resistance
order_blocks.entry_rule: Enter when price returns to order block with confirmation
order_blocks.validity: Order block remains valid until fully mitigated (price trades through it)

fair_value_gaps.definition: Imbalance in price where candle wicks don't overlap
fair_value_gaps.bullish_fvg: Gap between candle 1 high and candle 3 low (upward move)
fair_value_gaps.bearish_fvg: Gap between candle 1 low and candle 3 high (downward move)
fair_value_gaps.entry_rule: Price often returns to fill 50% of FVG before continuing
fair_value_gaps.confluence: FVG + Order Block = high probability setup

liquidity_pools.definition: Areas where stop losses cluster (equal highs/lows, round numbers)
liquidity_pools.sweep: Price moves to take liquidity then reverses
liquidity_pools.rule: Look for liquidity sweeps at key levels before entering counter move

london_open.description: High volatility, good for GBP and EUR pairs

new_york_open.description: Highest volume, best for USD pairs and indices

kill_zones.rule: Take trades only during London or New York kill zones for best probability

optimal_trade_entry.description: ICT's sweet spot for entries after impulse move
optimal_trade_entry.rule: Wait for price to retrace into OTE zone before entering

how_to_draw.uptrend: Draw from swing low to swing high
how_to_draw.downtrend: Draw from swing high to swing low
how_to_draw.rule: Use most recent significant swing points

key_levels.0.618: Golden ratio - PRIMARY entry zone (OTE start)
key_levels.0.786: Deep retracement - OTE end, last chance entry
key_levels.0.886: Very deep - trend may be weakening

entry_strategy.confirmation_required: Wait for bullish/bearish candle pattern at Fib level
entry_strategy.confluence: Fib level + Order Block + FVG = highest probability

entry_checklist.step_1: Identify HTF trend (Daily/4H) - only trade WITH the trend
entry_checklist.step_2: Wait for impulse move in trend direction (BOS)
entry_checklist.step_3: Draw Fibonacci from swing low to high (or vice versa)
entry_checklist.step_4: Identify order blocks and FVGs in the retracement path
entry_checklist.step_5: Wait for price to retrace into OTE zone (0.618-0.786)
entry_checklist.step_6: Look for confluence: OTE + Order Block + FVG
entry_checklist.step_7: Check if we're in a kill zone (London/NY session)
entry_checklist.step_8: Wait for entry confirmation (bullish/bearish engulfing, rejection wick)
entry_checklist.step_9: Set stop loss below/above the order block with buffer
entry_checklist.step_10: Set take profit for minimum 1:2 RR, aim for 1:3
entry_checklist.step_11: Enter trade only if ALL conditions are met

bullish_setup.confluence: Bullish order block + FVG in OTE zone
bullish_setup.confirmation: Bullish engulfing or hammer at support
bullish_setup.entry: Enter on close of confirmation candle

bearish_setup.confluence: Bearish order block + FVG in OTE zone
bearish_setup.confirmation: Bearish engulfing or shooting star at resistance
bearish_setup.entry: Enter on close of confirmation candle

partial_profits.second_target: Let remaining 50% run to 1:3 or higher
partial_profits.trailing_stop: Move stop to breakeven after 1:1.5 RR

trade_management.breakeven_rule: Move stop to entry +/- spread once trade is 1:1.5 in profit
trade_management.scaling_out: Close partial positions at key resistance/support levels
trade_management.holding_winners: Let winners run if trend remains strong and no reversal signals

bad_setups: Entering before retracement to OTE zone
Taking trades with less than 1:2 RR
Trading without order block or FVG confluence
emotional_rules: Never revenge trade after a loss
Stick to max 2-3 trades per day
If 2 losses in a row, stop trading for the day
Never increase position size after losses

pre_market: Check economic calendar for high-impact news
Identify HTF trend on Daily and 4H charts
Mark key liquidity levels (previous day high/low, equal highs/lows)
Identify existing order blocks and FVGs
during_session: Wait for kill zone (London or NY open)
Watch for impulse moves and BOS
Draw Fibonacci on new swing points
Wait patiently for price to reach OTE zone
Only enter with full confluence and confirmation
post_market: Journal all trades (setup, entry, exit, emotions)
Review what worked and what didn't
Update key levels for next day
Calculate win rate and average RR

performance_metrics.max_daily_loss: Stop trading after losing 4% of account in one day
performance_metrics.monthly_target: Aim for 10-20% monthly return with proper risk management

notes.patience: The best trades come to you. Wait for perfect setups.
notes.discipline: Follow the rules even when emotions say otherwise.
notes.consistency: Trade the same setup repeatedly to master it.
notes.learning: Every trade is a lesson. Journal and review regularly.
notes.reality: Not every day will have a setup. That's okay. Protect capital first.
